summary: LEGION-71 lands pull request #957's Fast-follow batch as one T4 pull request on the issue branch legion/LEGION-71: four files under scripts/smoke/, no change to what the rig does. Baseline on this branch (5db19570, main at planning time): up.test.sh passes 16/16 from the repository root and 0/16 from /tmp (the sourced copy resolves repo_root to / and bun happens to resolve //packages/... against the cwd); checkpoints.test.sh 21/21 and down.test.sh 3/3 pass from /tmp already. Eleven ordered tasks below; expected after implementation: up.test.sh 17 PASS from /tmp, checkpoints.test.sh 22 PASS from /tmp, down.test.sh 3 PASS from /tmp (unchanged, proves the directory claim for all three).

baseline.head: 5db19570 (chore: release cli v1.9.0), bookmark legion/LEGION-71 at 49397b02 (working copy, carries only the provisioned .omp/config.yml)
baseline.upTestFromTmp: exit 1, 0 PASS: `error: Module not found "//packages/daemon/src/daemon/omp-pin.ts"` then `error: could not read the OMP pin ...` — the sourced copy's repo_root is `/` (dirname of the mktemp file, ../..), so every repo_root path is `//packages/...`; bun resolves that only when cwd is the repository root.
baseline.upTestFromRoot: exit 0, 16 PASS (after `bun install --frozen-lockfile` in the workspace — a fresh workspace has no node_modules and the --check-config case fails with `Cannot find module '@legion/contracts'`; run bun install once before any harness run).
baseline.realMiseStderr: mise 2026.8.10 on this box: a missing pin prints `mise ERROR <pin> not installed` (+ version/verbose lines) exit 1; a broken config (MISE_CONFIG_FILE at a non-TOML file) prints `Error loading settings file: TOML parse error ...` and `mise::config::parse_error ... Invalid TOML in config file: <path>` exit 1 with no `not installed`; an unknown backend prints `mise ERROR <name> is not a valid plugin name`. Success may still print `mise WARN  GitHub rate limit exceeded` on stderr. Classifying on the substring `not installed` matches the real mise and the harness's existing fake.
baseline.shellcheck: shellcheck 0.11.0 on up.sh, up.test.sh, checkpoints.test.sh: exactly one pre-existing finding, SC2155 at up.sh:22 (`readonly smoke_actor_id="...$(date ...)"`), out of scope — leave it; the implementation must add no new finding.
baseline.prototypes: Planner prototyped on scratch copies outside the workspace (nothing committed): (a) pinning repo_root in the sourced copy alone takes up.test.sh from 0 to 16 PASS from /tmp; (b) with the three success-path main() calls in the `(set -e; …)` form and the fake `go` made to `exit 1`, the harness fails at the first main() (exit 1, 10 PASS) while the current `if !` form still passes 16/16 — that is the tester's negative control for acceptance 2; (c) the mise-branch shape in T1 passes WARN through on success, shows the remedy only for `not installed`, stops on mise's own message for a config error, and leaks no temp file.

alreadySatisfied: Acceptance 4, precedence behaviour: checkpoints.sh `stored_webhook_mode` (lines 59-68) already reads `${smoke_dir}/webhook-mode` first and consults SMOKE_WEBHOOK_MODE only when the file is absent. Only the test pin is missing (T9); checkpoints.sh is not edited.

Acceptance 5, pull-request numbers in comments: `grep -nE '#[0-9]{3,}'` over the four files finds them only in up.test.sh (lines 341 `pre-#941`, 343 `before #971`, 358 PASS line `pre-#941`). up.sh, checkpoints.test.sh and README.md carry none — nothing to do there.
Acceptance 2, checkpoints.test.sh and down.test.sh from /tmp: both already pass (21 and 3 PASS); only up.test.sh is directory-bound.
Everything else in acceptance 1-5 is not yet satisfied on this head (evidence per task below).

tasks.change: Rewrite the mise branch so mise's stderr is captured to a `mktemp` file, shown on the operator's stderr whatever the exit (a success-path WARN included), and the file removed before any exit path. On a non-zero exit: when the captured text contains `not installed`, `fail "OMP pin ${omp_pin} is not installed (mise where failed); run: mise install ${omp_pin}"` (unchanged text — the existing assertion pins `OMP pin <pin> is not installed` and `run: mise install <pin>`); otherwise `fail "mise where ${omp_pin} failed; mise's own message is above"` — no remedy. Keep the `bin/omp is missing or not executable; run: mise install <pin>` message as is. Shape the planner verified: `local mise_stderr mise_said; local mise_status=0; mise_stderr="$(mktemp)"; install_dir="$(mise where "$omp_pin" 2>"$mise_stderr")" || mise_status=$?; cat "$mise_stderr" >&2; mise_said="$(<"$mise_stderr")"; rm -f "$mise_stderr"; if ((mise_status != 0)); then [[ "$mise_said" != *'not installed'* ]] || fail "...not installed...; run: mise install ${omp_pin}"; fail "mise where ${omp_pin} failed; mise's own message is above"; fi`. Use bash pattern matching, not grep (up.sh does not require grep). Update the header comment: replace `exported to the daemon only (main's start_process env block)` with `the daemon's start_process env block in main() is the only place up.sh names it explicitly (the operator's own export reaches every child process as any exported variable does)`, and add one sentence: a pin that is not installed stops the rig naming `mise install <pin>`; any other `mise where` failure stops on mise's own message, without that remedy.
